details: Bitcoin has ascended above $81,000 for the first time in three months, propelled by several supportive macroeconomic factors. These include easing energy prices, a decline in US Treasury yields, a softer US dollar, and robust performance in US equity markets. Ethereum has also followed suit with gains, indicating that the cryptocurrency market is increasingly acting as a high-beta risk asset, benefiting from broader market liquidity and a "risk-on" sentiment among investors.
title: Bitcoin Surges Past $81,000 on Macro Tailwinds

details: The European Central Bank's (ECB) wage tracking indicator suggests that wage growth in the Eurozone is expected to decelerate to 2.6% in 2026, a decrease from 3% in 2025. This data, released by the ECB on Wednesday, is a critical metric for the central bank as it assesses inflationary pressures and contemplates future monetary policy adjustments. ECB officials are closely observing ongoing wage negotiations, with a hint of a potential interest rate hike in June if the current upward momentum in inflation persists.
title: ECB Indicator Predicts Slower Eurozone Wage Growth for 2026

details: François Villeroy de Galhau, an outgoing member of the European Central Bank's (ECB) Governing Council, maintains a dovish stance regarding interest rates, asserting that there is currently no sufficient justification for a rate hike. He believes that the impact of rising oil prices on inflation has not yet reached a level that would necessitate an increase in borrowing costs. This perspective contrasts with market sentiment, where traders are pricing in a 75-77% probability of a June rate hike. Despite Villeroy's comments, Eurozone consumer inflation expectations have climbed to 4.0%, marking the highest level since 2023.
sourceName: Moomoo (reporting on Zhitong Finance / Futu News)
title: Outgoing ECB Official Villeroy Sees No Immediate Need for Rate Hike
